hypothesis: A population of complete seven-row chromosomes can escape the clamped published-witness basin when row-level recombination is combined with conflict-directed coordinate repair, and may produce a validator-accepted scope-111 DTS.
rationale: The existing coordinate annealing remained at 100 unique differences and the independent valid-row library packing remained at 96-97, but neither method co-evolved row choices with a population and explicitly targeted rows responsible for duplicate differences. The proposed representation keeps every row as a six-mark Golomb ruler and uses exact global difference counts for selection, so it tests a materially different search dynamic without changing the mathematical target or verifier.
expected_information_gain: A validator-accepted seven-row assignment is direct true-objective progress. A reproducible best-score distribution above 100 would identify an escape from the known clamped basin; failure to exceed 100 across fixed seeds would close this population/recombination/coordinate-repair family at the declared budget, without implying global infeasibility.
method: Compile research_tools/search_dts_memetic.cpp with the pinned WSL2 g++ toolchain. For each of three fixed seeds, initialize a population of complete scope-111 internally valid six-mark rows with the clamped scope-112 witness included as an anchor. Repeatedly select tournament parents, recombine row genes, inject an occasional new valid row, and apply conflict-directed coordinate mutations: identify globally duplicated differences, preferentially mutate a row containing one, and sometimes target a currently missing difference. Retain exact global unique-difference fitness with row validity as a hard feasibility tier. Emit the best rows and independently validate any complete output with research_tools/verify_dts.py and research_tools/verify_dts_independent.py.
metric: Per-seed best unique positive differences out of 105, internal row validity, iterations, and independent validator result
metric_relation_to_true_objective: A complete validator-valid seven-row result with scope<=111 is exactly the frozen true objective. Unique-difference score below 105 and all runtime/iteration metrics are proxy evidence only.

configuration.initialization: random internally valid scope-111 Golomb rows plus clamped published scope-112 witness
configuration.repair: duplicate-row targeting plus one-coordinate mutation, with missing-difference targeting on half of repair proposals

kill_condition: Stop each seed at a validator-accepted target, at its 90-second wall budget, or at a precise runtime failure. Preserve all seed results. Do not interpret a finite best score or timeout as mathematical infeasibility.

baseline_comparison.expected_relation: strict improvement only if an independent validator accepts scope<=111

previous_best_comparison.expected_relation: population/recombination should be tested by best unique score and target reach, not by proxy score alone

interpretation: All three fixed-seed native runs converged to the same internally valid 103/105 state, improving the clamped anchor's 100/105 proxy score but failing both independent validators because differences 10 and 21 each occurred twice. No scope-111 target was reached.
what_was_learned: Population recombination and duplicate-directed coordinate repair escaped the clamped 100/105 state to 103/105, but the identical endpoint across three seeds indicates a stable basin rather than a complete construction. A deterministic local-neighborhood audit is more informative than another identical stochastic run.
recommended_next_action: Run the separately preregistered exhaustive one/two-coordinate neighborhood around this 103 state; if it misses, close this basin and do not repeat the same memetic settings.
repetition_justification: This is not a repeat of the earlier annealer or row-library packer: it introduces a population, row-gene crossover, stochastic row injection, and duplicate-directed coordinate repair in one deterministic native implementation.
